explanation: Your understanding is strong: quotes make the enclosed word a text value; without quotes, Python treats the word as a name and looks up its current value. Reassigning a name changes what later uses of that name refer to. One nuance: Python does not necessarily print a value just because it appears in quotes—printing happens when you use a print instruction. An unassigned name causes a NameError when Python tries to look it up; None is a value you can assign to a name.
